chapter: The China offer, wedding and Shanghai
title: Public executions of criminals
summary: He describes the beheadings of Chinese convicts at the slaughter grounds, which he never wanted to see.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: No, I kind of would like just to see it for maybe a day, but ......
I think Shanghai must have changed out of all recognition/███████ Hong Kong is probably a little like what China used to be. More like China used to be. but of course,

Yes. You know, we used to, so many strange things used to happen. I remember during that time if I wanted to go out to the slaughter grounds where they, they used to just chop people's heads off, criminals.
People that stole. People that killed, murdered. If you wanted to, at six o'clock in the morning I've seen big trucks full

of convicts and guards sitting on there with their guns down on them. They would take them out to this place and they got special men out there with these big axes, great big axes. And if you wanted to you could look at them.
And they'd chop off their heads. Put their heads up on posts..........
Well, that's like the middle ages.
Yes. And shoot them. I could hear the gun shot, but I never did want to go see them.
No, but some of the guys did I suppose.

Teddy Weatherford had been there; and they had experts with these axes. Guys could tie your hands together like that and just split your hands without touching your body like that. Guys cut off two, three heads at one time. And you could buy picture of it even.
If you didn't go see it yourself they would.......
This was not Japanese, this was Chinese?
This was Chinese against criminals, Chinese criminals. That's something. Strange you know.
Yes, I never did want to see it. I couldn't, I didn't even like to look at the pictures I saw of it.
